//: Template for the SHARED LIVE bucket. infra/provision-hosted.mjs substitutes __BUCKET__, __ACCOUNT__ and __DISTRIBUTION__. Kept in the repo because this policy is the thing standing between every tenant's site and the open internet, and it should be reviewable without reading a script.

Statement.//: The only read grant. Scoped to ONE distribution by SourceArn: without that condition, any CloudFront distribution in any AWS account could name this bucket as its origin and serve it. That is the confused-deputy hole in every OAC example that omits the condition.

The end-run guard. Deny unless the caller is a principal in OUR account, or is our distribution. An explicit Deny beats every Allow anywhere, so this holds even against a policy somebody adds later or an over-broad grant on some IAM role. Deliberately NOT written with NotPrincipal: NotPrincipal+Deny does not match assumed-role session ARNs against their role ARN, which is the classic way to lock yourself out of your own bucket. The two condition keys are ANDed, so a request is denied only when it is neither ours nor the CDN's -- and an anonymous request, which carries neither key, fails both tests and is denied.
